_comment_cta: URL dropped into the soft ask at the end of every assembled email, and rendered as the page's link button. Use THIS PRODUCT'S OWN domain — see config-oryoniq.json, which points at oryoniq.com for the same reason.
personalization_prompt: Write ONE specific opening line (max 2 sentences) for a cold email to {first_name}, {title} at {company} — a federal or SLED organization. Tie the current signal to their security/modernization mandate. Do NOT invent specific facts about {company}.
_comment_booking_url: A URL that can be EMBEDDED — Sendr's calendar element puts its value in an <iframe src>, which is why this is deliberately separate from `cta` (an ordinary link on a button). EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and a contact page is NOT a substitute: both www.visioneerit.com/contact and www.oryoniq.com/contact were re-tested 2026-08-17 and send `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` + `frame-ancestors 'self'`, so the browser refuses to render them and the page shows a grey broken-content box (seen live 2026-08-16 on both templates). Contact pages therefore belong in `cta`, on a link button — putting one here re-creates the exact bug. Until a real embeddable booking URL exists (Calendly, HubSpot Meetings, Cal.com — all designed to be framed), leave this empty and keep the calendar element REMOVED from the Sendr template. Filling it later also makes Sendr's `engagement:meeting_booked` event reachable, which VIO-sendr-events already routes to Slack as the goal state.

_comment_compliance: CAN-SPAM 15 U.S.C. 7704(a)(5) requires every commercial message to carry a valid physical postal address AND a working opt-out. Neither existed in any sendable body until 2026-08-30 — verified across all 10 steps of both campaigns. Liability is per message, so this is not something to add 'before launch'; it has to be in the copy the moment anything can send. The opt-out is REPLY-BASED on purpose rather than a merge tag: VIO-instantly-events already writes an opt_out event to the Suppression tab and VIO-inbound-reply-to-call already detects stop intent in reply text, both with registered webhooks — so this route is known to work, whereas an unverified merge tag can render as a literal token in a real prospect's inbox. Instantly's own insert_unsubscribe_header is turned on alongside it for one-click support. Both strings are mirrored into every campaign body; sync-routes.py's `compliance` check fails if any sendable body loses either one.
